request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:

A: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce duplicates provider refresh instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is silently bypassed for this integration
B: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-97 — Salesforce implements its own inline `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` refresh call and never calls `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, unlike googlecalendar, hubspot, larkcalendar, office365calendar, office365video, and webex which all route their refresh through `refreshOAuthTokens`; since `refreshOAuthTokens` is the gate that checks `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`/`CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and calls the new external credential-sync endpoint, Salesforce's credentials will silently never be synced via the new external endpoint feature that this diff's task ("OAuth credential sync") is supposed to deliver — this is an inconsistent, undocumented partial rollout within the very set of files this diff touches, not just a separate untouched integration.

A: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce duplicates provider refresh instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync is silently bypassed for this integration

PAIR 10:
A: SalesforceCalendarService now performs an unconditional token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every service construction, where the previous code used the stored access token and refreshed only when needed. Every Salesforce-backed booking create/update/delete now pays an extra round-trip to login.salesforce.com and a credential DB write on the hot path; under booking load this multiplies Salesforce token-endpoint calls (rate-limit risk turns into failed bookings) and adds latency the previous path did not have.
B: The newly added Salesforce token-refresh fetch and prisma.credential.update run unconditionally on every service construction, with no expiry check, on a hot path (every calendar operation instantiates the service). Every Salesforce calendar read/write now issues an external token HTTP call plus a DB write even when the stored token is still valid, adding latency and provider rate-limit pressure to the booking path for all Salesforce users.

A: New non-trivial sync/refresh logic (refreshOAuthTokens contract, parseRefreshTokenResponse placeholder behavior, the webhook handler's create/update branching) ships with no tests anywhere in the diff. The exact failure modes above (Response-shape mismatches, placeholder refresh_token, wrong-user sync) are precisely the regressions no existing suite would catch, and each deployment with credential sharing enabled hits them on the first token expiry.
B: The diff adds a new authenticated write API endpoint and two new shared OAuth utilities (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse) that alter the token-refresh path of eight integrations, with zero test files or assertions anywhere in the diff (no spec/test/itest-shaped file appears in the changed paths). A regression in the placeholder refresh_token mutation or the raw-Response return type (both present in this diff) would break every booking on the affected integrations and ship undetected; there is no verification of the webhook's auth rejection, schema validation, or create-vs-update branch, and no fixture proving the sync endpoint contract (fetch body shape, response shape) matches what all eight call sites expect.
